claims.text: The starting material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
Grain refinement introduces lattice defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
Introducing unspecified alloying elements introduces lattice defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect-induced phonon scattering reduces the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity.
Grain refinement would reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Introducing unspecified alloying elements would reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The prediction is bounded to temperatures from approximately 0 to 200 K.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the specific grain-refinement or alloying method.
Thermal conductivity, lattice parameter, and grain size would be measured in modified and unchanged HfNbTaTiZr.
Failure of the intervention to reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is not singular or operationally fixed: grain refinement and alloying are distinct alternatives. The falsification rule concerns the lattice contribution, but the listed measurements include only total thermal conductivity and no electrical-resistivity or other electronic-transport measurement needed to separate lattice and electronic contributions.
